nodes.title: SG-6.1.3 Validate scene characters against the world's character list
nodes.body:
Context: validateWorld in game/src/content/loader.ts checks dialogue speakers and say events against world.characters, but never checks scene.characters (SceneDef.characters?: CharacterSpec[]). Desired behavior: each scene character id is checked against the world's list and unknown ids are reported as scenes[<sceneId>].characters[<index>].id: unknown character <id>. Expected result: dangling NPC references fail world content validation, and unit tests cover the reject and accept cases. Why: scene NPCs must reference declared world characters.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene character whose id is not in world.characters, when validateWorld runs, then the errors contain scenes[<sceneId>].characters[<index>].id: unknown character <id>
- Given a scene whose characters are all in world.characters, when validateWorld runs, then no character error is reported
- Given the unit tests in game/tests/validator.test.ts, when they run, then the reject and accept cases pass with every dependency mocked


## Scope
- In scope: validateWorld scene character check
- In scope: unit tests in game/tests/validator.test.ts
- Out of scope: characterSchema changes
- Out of scope: BootScene rendering
- Out of scope: dialogue speaker validation changes
- Preserve: existing unknown character message format for dialogue speakers and say events
- Preserve: existing validator tests


## Technical constraints
- Reuse the existing characters Set in validateWorld
- Do not change the error strings that already exist


## Definition of done
- Unknown scene character ids are reported with the path-tagged message
- Unit tests pass


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · validateWorld reports unknown scene character ids with a path-tagged issue
nodes.body:
Context: validateWorld iterates scenes but skips scene.characters. Desired behavior: for each scene and each index, an id missing from the world's character list adds scenes[<sceneId>].characters[<index>].id: unknown character <id>. Expected result: world content validation fails on dangling NPC ids and passes on valid ones. Why: prevents NPCs referencing undeclared characters.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given scene bedroom with characters [{id:'ghost'}] and a world listing only boy, when validateWorld runs, then errors contain 'scenes[bedroom].characters[0].id: unknown character ghost'
- Given a scene whose characters are all listed in world.characters, when validateWorld runs, then errors is empty
- Given a scene with no characters field, when validateWorld runs, then no character error is added


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/content/loader.ts validateWorld
- Out of scope: schema changes
- Preserve: existing validation behavior


## Technical constraints
- scene.characters is optional


## Definition of done
- Check implemented and unit tested


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Check scene characters in validateWorld
nodes.body:
In game/src/content/loader.ts validateWorld, inside the for (const scene of world.scenes) loop, iterate scene.characters ?? [] with index and push a path-tagged error for ids not in the existing characters Set.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unknown scene character ids push scenes[<sceneId>].characters[<index>].id: unknown character <id>
- Known ids and scenes without characters push nothing


## Scope
- In scope: validateWorld in game/src/content/loader.ts
- Out of scope: tests
- Preserve: existing checks


## Technical constraints
- Use the existing characters Set
- Code path: `game/src/content/loader.ts`


## Definition of done
- validateWorld reports unknown scene character ids


## Clarifying questions
- None
